It's been pointed out a couple of times that the Batman titles have been obliterating comic books sales. My question is, why is that? It can't be crossover from the movies, because DC's theatrical releases have been crap. I'm not aware of any animated series that they have currently running which might contribute. And it can't just be Batman as a character driving it, since multiple titles that don't necessarily feature him are right up there on the board and ahead of titles with the Holy Trinity (Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman).

Do all the Batbooks share the same writer or artist or something?
Why ARE Batman titles doing so well?

I'd primarily say it's been Scott Snyder's 5+ year run on Batman. He started on Detective Comics 871 through 881 (which gave us the Black Mirror and the Last Joker story).

He took Detective Comics which was basically the worst Batman title at the time and got some decent movement out of it before the New 52.

He then switched over to Batman when the New 52 started and he a ridiculously phenomenal run through all 52 issues there and after a few weeks of being #2 behind Justice League, went of to be the best selling DC title for virtually every remaining issue.

The stories he did on that title included the Court of Owls/Night of Owls, Death of the Family, Zero Year, Endgame, and Superheavy. Also the art of Greg Capullo was incredible on that title as well. For reference there were only about 7 issues of the New 52 Batman run that weren't included in one of those 5 storylines. (He also partially wrote Batman Eternal, which was a 52 issue weekly comic with another great storyline.)

He's currently doing All-Star Batman with John Romita Jr and you can tell DC knows exactly how important Snyder is because virtually every other DC title is $2.99 cover price, but All-Star Batman is $4.99 cover price. (Also JR JR brings a lot of quality to the title too, since his art on Superman Unchained dethroned the New 52 Batman as the best selling DC title for a few months.)

A lot of his work has crossed over into other Bat titles and has elevated a lot of writing in those titles, like Tim Seeley's work on Grayson and currently Nightwing, James Tynion IV's work on Detective Comics, or Tom King's work on Batman after replacing Scott Snyder. Not so coincidentally, Seely and Tynion both worked with Snyder on Batman Eternal.

tl;dr, Scott Snyder is mother fucking God to Batman fans right now.
